section.title: Search Endpoint
section.question: Line 4 builds a SQL string by interpolating params[:q] directly into it — what's the vulnerability and how would you mitigate it?
section.snippet:
class SearchController < ApplicationController
  def index
    term = params[:q]
    sql = "SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%#{term}%'"
    @results = Product.find_by_sql(sql)
    render json: @results
  end
end
section.teaching_note: Think about what params[:q] could contain besides a search term.

reference.tagline: A string built by interpolating user input into SQL is a vulnerability, not a query.
reference.explanation: Interpolating params[:q] directly into the SQL string lets an attacker supply SQL syntax instead of a search term, changing what the query does rather than just what it matches.
reference.code_example:
# Vulnerable — the attacker's input becomes part of the query itself
Product.find_by_sql("SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%#{term}%'")

# Safe — the placeholder is bound as data, never parsed as SQL
Product.where("name LIKE ?", "%#{term}%")
reference.senior_lens: Any user-controlled value reaching a query string has to be bound as a parameter, never interpolated — that rule holds whether the string is built with find_by_sql, a raw SQL fragment, or string concatenation elsewhere in the app.
